comments.note: SECURITY NOTE for Security Auditor: when gitResult.exitCode !== 0, the error field is set to `gitResult.stderr` directly. If the cloneUrl had a token injected (e.g., https://ghp_token@github.com/org/repo.git), git may include the token-bearing URL in stderr ('fatal: repository https://ghp_token@github.com/...' not found'). The error propagates via OrchestrationRepoResult.error to the GUI toast (WP-005). stripEmbeddedCredentials() should be called on gitResult.stderr before assigning to the error field. This is out of scope for WP-006 ACs but must be addressed before release.

summary: Reviewed 2 files (workspace-orchestrator.ts, repository-orchestrator.ts). 0 Critical. 1 High — token leak via unstripped git stderr. Routes back to Developer for remediation.

comments.note: HIGH — A02 (Cryptographic Failures) / A09 (Security Logging & Monitoring Failures). File: src/orchestration/workspace-orchestrator.ts:129 and src/orchestration/repository-orchestrator.ts:128. When gitResult.exitCode !== 0, the raw gitResult.stderr is assigned directly to the OrchestrationRepoResult/WorkspaceCloneResult error field without sanitization. git routinely includes the full clone URL in fatal error messages (e.g. 'fatal: repository https://ghp_TOKEN@github.com/org/repo not found'). This error propagates via sendJson(res, 200, result) → HTTP JSON response → GUI toast, exposing the token to any API consumer and browser context. The stripEmbeddedCredentials() utility is already exported from src/git/git-credentials.ts and is exactly suited to fix this. Remediation: in both orchestrators replace `error: gitResult.stderr || ...` with `error: stripEmbeddedCredentials(gitResult.stderr) || ...`, and import stripEmbeddedCredentials from '../git/git-credentials.js'.

MEDIUM — A01 (Broken Access Control). File: src/orchestration/workspace-orchestrator.ts, createWorkspace() — the fs.rmSync() call on a leftover clone directory does not apply the same path-traversal guard that RepositoryOrchestrator.addRepositoryToProject() applies (resolvedDest.startsWith check). Mitigating factor: repoId values are validated as kebab-case ([a-z0-9-] only), making traversal via stored IDs implausible under normal operation. The inconsistency should be resolved for defence-in-depth. Recommendation: add the same path.resolve() / startsWith() guard before the fs.rmSync() in createWorkspace().

INFO — A09 (Security Logging). stripEmbeddedCredentials() is exported and tested but never called in any production code path. This is the root cause of the High finding. A lint/grep CI check requiring stripEmbeddedCredentials() to be applied anywhere gitResult.stderr flows to an API response would prevent regression.

summary: Re-audit of reworked WP-006 (workspace-orchestrator.ts, repository-orchestrator.ts). 0 Critical. 1 High — the previous High finding (token leak via git stderr) is NOT resolved. comments.note: HIGH — A02 (Cryptographic Failures) / A09 (Security Logging & Monitoring Failures). Previous High finding NOT resolved — remediation is semantically incorrect. Files: src/orchestration/workspace-orchestrator.ts (~L136) and src/orchestration/repository-orchestrator.ts (~L130). The fix calls `stripEmbeddedCredentials(gitResult.stderr)` expecting it to scrub token-bearing URLs from a git error message, but `stripEmbeddedCredentials` is a URL sanitizer: it calls `new URL(input)` and strips userinfo from the parsed URL. When git fails, stderr is a prose string such as `"fatal: repository 'https://ghp_TOKEN@github.com/org/repo.git/' not found"` — this is NOT a valid URL, so `new URL(...)` throws, the catch block returns the ORIGINAL string unchanged, and the token is passed through unmodified to the API response. Evidence: git-credentials.ts catch block `return url;`; test `stripEmbeddedCredentials() returns malformed URL unchanged` confirms this behavior with `'not-a-url'` returning `'not-a-url'`. Remediation (two equivalent options): Option A — omit stderr from the error field entirely and use only `git clone exited with code ${gitResult.exitCode}` (most secure, no leakage possible); Option B — apply a regex scrub before assigning: `gitResult.stderr.replace(/https?:\/\/[^@\s]*@/g, 'https://***@')`. Either approach must be applied in both orchestrators.

All other areas reviewed clean. Path-traversal guard (Medium from previous audit) is correctly implemented in both orchestrators with path.resolve() / startsWith(resolvedProjectsFolder + path.sep) pattern. injectCredentials() uses WHATWG URL API for token injection (safe, percent-encodes special characters). GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and GIT_ASKPASS=echo environment guards are correctly set in git-cli.ts. No token is written to the repositories.json data model. No other OWASP A01–A10 issues identified beyond the active High finding.

summary: [REWORK] Resolved Security Auditor High finding (A02/A09 — token leak in git stderr). Root cause: `stripEmbeddedCredentials()` used `new URL()` to parse its input; the WHATWG URL parser accepts prose strings like git error messages (e.g. `fatal: repository '...'`) by treating the leading word as a URL scheme (e.g. `fatal:`), so the URL-parsing try block succeeded, the `protocol !== 'https:'` guard fired, and the original string was returned unchanged — carrying the embedded token. Fix: restructured the function to fall through to a regex scrub `(https?:\\/\\/)[^@\\s]*@` → `$1***@` for any input where the parsed protocol is not `https:` (including the WHATWG-accepted prose strings and genuine parse failures). Pure HTTPS URLs still go through the URL-object path for clean credential stripping. Added 2 new regression tests (`scrubs token from git prose error message`, `scrubs multiple embedded URLs in a single prose message`). All 608 tests pass, zero build errors."]

comments.note: src/git/git-credentials.ts — stripEmbeddedCredentials(): the WHATWG URL parser silently accepts prose strings with a word-like prefix (e.g. `fatal: …`) by treating the prefix as a custom scheme. This is a subtle gotcha that is easy to overlook in security-sensitive sanitisers. Added an explanatory inline comment and restructured control flow so non-HTTPS inputs correctly fall through to regex scrubbing.
